results.title: Patient Inclusion & Exclusion Criteria: Safety Vs Representation
results.content: Patient Inclusion & Exclusion Criteria: Safety Vs Representation. ### Patient Inclusion & Exclusion Criteria: Safety Vs Representation. Designing the right inclusion and exclusion criteria for clinical trials is perhaps one of the most consequential aspects of protocol development. At Nclusiv, we've observed how unnecessarily restrictive criteria can drastically limit recruitment pools and produce findings that fail to represent real-world patient populations. Conversely, criteria that are too permissive may introduce safety risks or compromise data integrity. The Evolution of Inclusion/Exclusion Criteria. Protocol authors often borrow criteria from previous studies without critically evaluating their relevance to the current research question. Are your trial criteria unnecessarily limiting your recruitment potential?**Nclusiv's protocol review service evaluates your inclusion/exclusion criteria to identify opportunities for greater inclusivity without compromising safety or data integrity.**. Rather than beginning with an exhaustive list of exclusions, start with the minimum criteria necessary for safety and scientific validity. Add additional criteria only when clearly justified by safety data or study objectives. Formal assessment of how your criteria might affect different demographic groups is essential for developing inclusive protocols. At Nclusiv, our Equality Impact Assessments evaluate criteria against demographic data to identify potentially discriminatory effects. Patients offer invaluable insights into how inclusion/exclusion criteria might affect recruitment and participation. Nclusiv's patient focus groups have repeatedly identified criteria that create unnecessary barriers to participation, helping sponsors develop more accessible protocols without compromising safety. Consider implementing adaptive criteria that can be adjusted as safety data accumulates during the trial. Effective criteria in oncology require especially careful balancing of scientific objectives, safety concerns, and the urgent needs of patients with limited options. When developing criteria for pediatric studies:. **In rare disease research, overly restrictive criteria can make recruitment practically impossible while undermining the very purpose of the study.**. Developing truly balanced inclusion/exclusion criteria requires moving beyond traditional approaches to embrace a more nuanced evaluation of risk and representation. At Nclusiv, our approach combines regulatory expertise, patient perspectives, and EDI principles to help sponsors develop criteria that protect participants while maximizing representation. results.content: Inclusion/exclusion criteria development is critical for determining a patients eligibility to participate in a clinical trial. Therefore, one might exclude patients with concomitant disease which could confound results; or patients of certain age (e.g., to exclude or include pediatric patients); or patients for whom the device is not appropriately sized. Or, a patient may have exactly the right indication to be treated with the device under study, but if there is no size of the device that is appropriate for the patient’s anatomy, that patient must be excluded. If the patient has any of the exclusion criteria, s/he must be excluded from the study. To state it another way, an inclusion criterion is sufficient all by itself for a patient to be treated with the device (i.e., the patient has the condition for which the device is indicated). In contrast, while an exclusion criterion is sufficient all by itself to exclude a patient from the study, its inverse is not sufficient to include a patient.

Inclusion and exclusion criteria should not leave room for different interpretations; they should clearly define who is and who isn’t eligible for participation in a study. results.title: Inclusion and Exclusion Criteria in Clinical Research - Suburban Research Associates
results.content: # Inclusion and Exclusion Criteria in Clinical Research. Have you ever applied for a research study only to be told you were not eligible? We must assess each potential patient for what is called inclusion and exclusion criteria for every study; and for each of them, that criteria is different. Inclusion criteria is criteria that must be met for a person to be eligible to participate in the study. Exclusion criteria is criteria that if a person meets, they would then not be eligible for the study. All research studies and clinical trials have these criteria in place. **What if I am not eligible for a study?**. If you have applied for a study that you weren’t eligible for, there is always a possibility that a new study will start with different criteria; as research is evolving every single day. You can also always talk to your medical and/or mental health care team to discuss different options that might be able to help if you are unable to participate in a research study.
